item.title: SCMP: More than 50% of Americans believe China is winning. So does the rest of the world
item.description: More than half of Americans believe China has already overtaken or will eventually surpass the United States in technology, economic strength and even military power, according to a study based on US public opinion data. The proportions reached 68.8 per cent in technology, 65.2 per cent in economic strength and 58.3 per cent in military power. The findings could have implications for China’s strategy towards Washington, as most American respondents no longer assume their country will retain…

item.title: SCMP: China busts cross-border blood smuggling ring over biosecurity fears
item.description: China has cracked down on the smuggling of blood samples from pregnant women, highlighting what authorities describe as a threat to national biosecurity. State broadcaster CCTV reported on Wednesday that Shenzhen Customs anti-smuggling officers had dismantled an underground network that illegally collected and transported the blood out of mainland China. The samples were used for fetal sex determination, a practice banned on the mainland for non-medical purposes. Following a nearly year-long...

item.title: SCMP: Japan plans new long-range anti-ship missile to bolster naval build-up
item.description: Tokyo is planning to introduce a new long-range anti-ship missile that could be launched from a broader range of vessels, according to Japanese media reports, potentially complicating Chinese military planning in a conflict. The proposed capability could allow Japan to equip vessels that traditionally do not carry anti-ship missiles, according to defence experts. The country is also looking to deploy a persistent surveillance system in medium Earth orbit to improve its ability to detect and...

item.title: SCMP: Shenzhen’s Apec legacy: China’s shift from recognition to responsibility
item.description: As the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit concluded in Shenzhen, one question rose above the diplomacy and symbolism: what does China’s growing global influence now require of it? For much of the past four decades, China’s paramount goal was integration. It sought access to markets, technology, investment and institutions to fuel its modernisation and development. item.title: SCMP: Will Solomon Islands’ Australia treaty prompt China to rethink its Pacific strategy?
item.description: The Solomon Islands’ decision to replace its 2022 security pact with China with a sweeping new Australian treaty may push Beijing to rethink its Pacific playbook, observers say. While some analysts said Honiara’s pivot reflected hard-nosed domestic pragmatism rather than a regional rush to shut out Beijing, others warned that Beijing must be wary of Canberra using the pact as a foothold to extend exclusive demands from security into economic and development ties. item.title: SCMP: China and Netherlands send ‘positive signal’ over global controls on military AI
item.description: China and the Netherlands have agreed on the need for international regulations on the military use of AI, a move hailed as an encouraging step forward. The two countries agreed on the necessity of global cooperation on artificial intelligence and the opportunities and risks from the technology, according to a joint statement issued on Wednesday after Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met his Dutch counterpart Tom Berendsen in Beijing. item.title: SCMP: PLA overhauls joint training after drills expose coordination gaps
item.description: China’s military is overhauling how its various services train together as joint exercises continue to expose shortcomings in the People’s Liberation Army’s ability to fight as an integrated force. In the latest example, a navy destroyer flotilla under the PLA’s Eastern Theatre Command changed how it trains with other services following drills in which airforce jets were twice judged to have been “shot down” by friendly forces. item.title: SCMP: Shanghai party chief’s downfall shows reach of anti-corruption drive
item.description: Shanghai’s Communist Party chief, Chen Jining, was placed under investigation for corruption as China’s widening anti-corruption drive toppled a fourth Politburo member ahead of a major leadership reshuffle next year. Chen is suspected of “serious breaches of discipline and law”, state broadcaster CCTV reported on Tuesday, using a common euphemism for corruption. item.title: SCMP: What others can learn from China’s effective governance
item.description: To understand China today, one must understand the Communist Party of China. The close attention the world paid to the fifth plenum of the 20th party congress, held in Beijing last month, underscores the global significance and contemporary relevance of this century-old party’s experience in self-supervision and self-governance. These are strands of historical DNA running through the entire course of the party. The plenary session noted that the party has achieved one victory after another...

item.title: SCMP: How China’s leadership will weigh up its choices for picking Shanghai’s next party chief
item.description: Beijing is considering its options for the next Shanghai party boss following the sudden downfall of Chen Jining. His ousting breaks decades of precedent and leaves a high-stakes vacuum in the country’s main financial hub less than a year before the 21st Communist Party congress, where there is likely to be a major leadership reshuffle. item.title: SCMP: Taiwan’s main opposition Kuomintang faces uphill battle in local elections
item.description: Taiwan’s main opposition Kuomintang (KMT) faces an uphill battle in Saturday’s local elections, with its goal of retaining 15 local administrations looking increasingly difficult to achieve. What was once expected to be a relatively comfortable election season for the KMT has turned into a critical test of its political strength, campaign strategies and internal unity ahead of the island’s 2028 leadership race. item.title: SCMP: China’s anti-corruption campaign tracker
item.description: China’s top graft-buster has ensnared 61 senior civilian officials so far this year, including two sitting Politburo members, according to a tally by the SCMP.
